simple.meaning: אַשְׁדּוֹד (ʼAshdôwd) appears 17 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced in connection with priesthood. The occurrence trail connects the name with an offering.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in Joshua, 1 Samuel, 2 Chronicles, Isaiah, Jeremiah, and 3 more, beginning at Joshua 11:22. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as offering, priesthood, land, Egypt, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אַשְׁדּוֹד (H795) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows אַשְׁדּוֹד through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.
simple.summary: אַשְׁדּוֹד (ʼAshdôwd) / H795 is tracked through Joshua 11:22, Joshua 15:46, Joshua 15:47, 1 Samuel 5:1. The entry is generated from source alignment, occurrence evidence, and the surrounding Scripture context.

timeline.evidenceText: There were none of the Anakim left in the land of the children of Israel. Only in Gaza, in Gath, and in Ashdod, did some remain.
from Ekron even to the sea, all that were by the side of Ashdod, with their villages.
Ashdod, its towns and its villages; Gaza, its towns and its villages; to the brook of Egypt, and the great sea with its coastline.
Now the Philistines had taken God’s ark, and they brought it from Ebenezer to Ashdod.
Therefore neither the priests of Dagon nor any who come into Dagon’s house step on the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod to this day.
But Yahweh’s hand was heavy on the people of Ashdod, and he destroyed them and struck them with tumors, even Ashdod and its borders.
When the men of Ashdod saw that it was so, they said, “The ark of the God of Israel shall not stay with us, for his hand is severe on us and on Dagon our god.”
These are the golden tumors which the Philistines returned for a trespass offering to Yahweh: for Ashdod one, for Gaza one, for Ashkelon one, for Gath one, for Ekron one;
He went out and fought against the Philistines, and broke down the wall of Gath, the wall of Jabneh, and the wall of Ashdod; and he built cities in the country of Ashdod, and among the Philistines.
He went out and fought against the Philistines, and broke down the wall of Gath, the wall of Jabneh, and the wall of Ashdod; and he built cities in the country of Ashdod, and among the Philistines.
In the year that Tartan came to Ashdod, when Sargon the king of Assyria sent him, and he fought against Ashdod and took it;
In the year that Tartan came to Ashdod, when Sargon the king of Assyria sent him, and he fought against Ashdod and took it;
and all the mixed people, and all the kings of the land of Uz, all the kings of the Philistines, Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and the remnant of Ashdod;
I will cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod,
Proclaim in the palaces at Ashdod,
For Gaza will be forsaken, and Ashkelon a desolation. They will drive out Ashdod at noonday, and Ekron will be rooted up.

definitions.full: H795. Ashdod אַשְׁדּוֺד proper name, of a location Ashdod (Assyrian Asdudu , COT Gloss Dl Pa 289 ; Thes MV derive from √ שׁדד q. v.) a powerful city of the Philistines on Mediterranean Sea, west from Jerusalem, modern Esdûd , Josh 11:22 ; 15:46-47 , (where assigned to Judah) 1Sam 5:5-6 , (but strike out Dr compare ᵐ5 ) 6:17 ; Amos 1:8 ; 3:9 ; Zeph 2:4 ; Zech 9:6 ; Isa 20:1 ; Jer 25:20 ; 2Chr 26:6 with ָ ה locative 1Sam 5:1 ; Isa 20:1 ; א ׳אַנְשֵׁי 1Sam 5:7 ; apparently = territory of Ashdod 2Chr 26:6 בְּאַשְׁדּוֺד עָרִים וַיִּבְנֶה . (compare Survey J, 442 .)
